2. Short facts for the disposal of the Rule may be stated as under: 

 5. Defendant Nos. 3Ka and 3Kha contested the suit by filing a joint written statement, contending, inter-alia, that the suit property, comprising Holding No.9/1 fell in the Saham of Gopal Chandra Basak by way of partition and after his death his son Tokani Lal Basak sold his share of the property in holding No.9/1 to Manna Lal Basak by registered Kabala dated 13-12-39 Ext. C(I) who in turn sold the same to the defendant No.2 by registered kabala dated 11-1-51 Ext. C(2). Thereafter, in 1978, defendant No.2 transferred the same to defendant Nos. 3Ka and 3Ka by registered deed of sale and since then they have been in possession. 

 12. Supporting the finding of the trial Court, Mr. Shamsuddin Ahmed, submits that the deed of lease dated 4-12-87 (Exhibit 1) and the subsequent deed of sale of the rent receiving interest (Exhibit 2) have no validity in the eye of law as the lease deed dated 4-12-57 has contravened the provisions of section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which has provided that: 

 Having shown that notification as stated in section 75A was published long before the execution of the aforesaid lease deed the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that as per section 47 of the Registration Act a document which requires to be registered, even if registered at a subsequent date, takes effect from the date of its execution and accordingly, the deed of permanent lease (Exhibit 1) took effect from the date of its execution. i.e. on 4-12-57 and that being so, it has been hit by section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 13. Mr. Md. Nurul Huq the learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party, hardly disputes that as per section 47 of the Registration Act a document which is required to be registered at a date subsequent to the date of execution after registration it takes effect from the date of execution and not from the date of registration but he submits that permanent lease unless registered is simply non est. Accordingly, a document which requires registration is created on the date of execution. In the present case both the deeds were registered together on 10-12-57, as such, he submitted that both deeds have to be considered together so as to ascertain the intention of the parties and to give any real meaning to the deeds these have to be considered together and if so considered together it would appear that these are not hit by section 75A of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act. In support of his argument he has cited 4 decisions.(I) the case of Messrs. Green & White Ltd. vs. Registrar, Joint Stock Companies, East Pakistan, reported in 15 DLR 492,(2) the case of the Province of East Pakistan vs. Muhammad Hossain Mia, reported in 16 DLR (SC) 667, (3) the case of Abdul Layes vs. Anwara Khatun and others, reported in 29 DLR (SC) 13 and (4) the case of Rafiqul Islam vs. Mir Abdul Ali, reported in 44 DLR (AD) 176. 

 15. In the case of Abul La yes, vs. Mst. Anwara Khatun, and others reported in 29 DLR (SC) 13. it was found by the Hon'ble Court that a lease dated 8-8-56 in respect of a premises followed by a deed of sale of rent with regard to that premises was a complete sale of the premises in law. Section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was not applicable. 

 In view of all the above observations I have no hesitation to hold that under the facts and circumstances of the present case, the deed of permanent lease executed by the defendant Nos. 4-8 on 4-12-57, followed by a deed of sale of the rent receiving interest executed on 9-12-57, and both being registered on 10-12-57 simultaneously, constituted a complete sale. Accordingly it has not been hit by section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 26. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners lastly submits that the plaintiff in his plaint claimed suit land comprising in holding Nos. 9/I and 9/2 and as such he contends that the plaintiff has no right to abandon his claim as regards holding No. 9/2, This submissions has hardly any legal basis. For the reasons stated above I do not find any ground for interference in this Rule.
